channels.name: Local OpenAI-compatible server
channels.audience: Cline, OpenCode and any OpenAI-compatible client
channels.summary: The OpenAI-compatible surface exists, but --ckpt is required at startup and there is no canonical checkpoint to load. It cannot serve a usable Taksh model yet.

evidence.unavailable_behavior: GET /v1/models returns an empty list with unavailable_reason; POST /v1/chat/completions returns HTTP 503

missing: canonical checkpoint loaded with --ckpt
tool-calling and streaming support for agentic clients
capability evaluation of the served model
security review before exposing beyond localhost
channels.first_action: Start the server only when a canonical checkpoint exists; keep it bound to localhost.

channels.name: Cline (VS Code coding agent)
channels.audience: Developers using Cline with a custom OpenAI-compatible provider
channels.summary: Cline can point at an OpenAI-compatible base URL, but Taksh rejects tool calls. Cline's agentic coding loop therefore cannot run against Taksh today, even if a checkpoint is loaded.

evidence.model_identifier: read from GET /v1/models after the server loads a checkpoint

missing: canonical checkpoint
tool-calling support or a documented chat-only mode
end-to-end request test from Cline
documented context window and tool-calling limitations
channels.first_action: Document the base URL and model id; test only against a canonical checkpoint.

channels.name: OpenRouter
channels.audience: Users of a hosted, paid model marketplace
channels.summary: OpenRouter lists models served by hosting providers; it does not run a local checkpoint. Taksh has no hosted endpoint, no pricing/terms decision and no capability evidence, so no listing can be submitted.
missing: hosted inference endpoint or provider partnership
commercial terms and pricing decision
capability and safety evidence suitable for a public listing
owner authorization to publish or submit
channels.first_action: Do not submit. Revisit only after a hosted, evaluated model exists.

verdict.statement: Taksh is not publishable as a model or dataset, and it is not ready for agentic coding clients. Only the source package and a chat-only local OpenAI-compatible surface are prepared, and neither may be published without explicit owner authorization.
